resources.title: Banana-leaf business
resources.subtitle: Explore sourcing, selling and the steps between.
resources.description: A starting point for exploring banana-leaf sourcing and export. Read the guide, find useful tools and choose the resources you need.

sections.title: Understand the opportunity
sections.intro: Start with the customer and work back to the supply. Choose a leaf format and a delivery route before approaching suppliers.

points.title: Who would you sell to?
points.text: Define your buyer: a distributor, retailer, restaurant or another business. Record their product and delivery requirements.

points.title: What would you supply?
points.text: Specify fresh, frozen or dried leaves; whole or cut size; grade; packing; and order quantity. These details make supplier quotes easier to compare.

points.title: What needs checking?
points.text: Confirm demand, handling requirements, total delivered cost and destination rules before committing to an order. Rules for banana fruit should not be assumed to cover banana leaves.

sections.title: Build your sourcing shortlist
sections.intro: Use the same questions with each supplier so you can compare the answers side by side.

points.title: Product and location
points.text: Record the supplier’s business identity, sourcing location and the exact product offered.

points.title: Order and delivery
points.text: Ask about minimum quantities, samples, packing, lead times and transport arrangements.

points.title: Evidence and follow-up
points.text: Keep dated quotes and record what has been checked directly. A listed contact alone does not establish supplier reliability.

sections.title: Map the costs
sections.intro: A useful costing sheet separates the purchase price from all the other costs of fulfilling the order.

points.title: Purchase and preparation
points.text: Allow space for product cost, grading, packaging and local transport.

points.title: Delivery and other charges
points.text: Record freight, handling, applicable documentation costs and any other quoted charges.

points.title: Your selling price
points.text: Compare total costs with the proposed selling price. Keep assumptions visible and replace estimates with current quotes.

sections.title: Prepare for buyer conversations
sections.intro: Before contacting a potential buyer, put the details they need in one place.

points.title: A clear product specification
points.text: Describe the product, packaging, quantity and delivery terms you can actually offer.

points.title: An organised enquiry
points.text: Ask about the buyer’s requirements, purchasing process and sample expectations.

points.title: A record of next steps
points.text: Keep track of enquiries, replies, quotations and the next agreed action.

sections.title: Your starting checklist
checklist: Identify a target buyer and their requirements
Check handling, transport and destination requirements
Decide the next step using the evidence collected
